methodological_rigor.justification: Large single-institution retrospective cohort (n=1290, OBCS 307 vs LNR 983) over 12 years (2008-2020) from a prospectively maintained database. Strengths include explicit STROBE adherence statement, clear inclusion/exclusion criteria, dual-reviewer data abstraction with third-reviewer adjudication, pre-specified primary and secondary outcomes, and consistent follow-up through 31 December 2021 with reportedly no losses. Weaknesses include substantial baseline imbalance between groups (OBCS patients younger, larger tumours, more multifocal disease, more neoadjuvant therapy) without propensity score matching or multivariable adjustment; complications recorded at patient level without attribution to specific breast; DFS only, no breast-cancer-specific survival; and the OBCS group has significantly shorter follow-up (4.64 vs 5.54 years).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Large-scale (reportedly largest Canadian) real-world comparison of OBCS vs lumpectomy with reasonable follow-up directly addresses a concern frequently cited by surgeons and patients (delay to adjuvant therapy and oncologic safety of OBCS). Findings (equivalent DFS, similar major complications, slightly longer time to radiotherapy, higher minor complication rates) support continued use and informed consent discussions. Classified Oxford LoE 2b as a retrospective cohort from a prospectively maintained database (individual cohort study).

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE guideline adherence is explicitly stated, and most STROBE items (setting, participants, variables, outcomes, data sources, bias/confounding discussion, flow of patients in Figure 1) are clearly reported. Clinicopathologic variables and outcome definitions are well-specified. Gaps include: no STROBE checklist appendix, patient-level complication attribution ambiguity, no explicit handling of missing data beyond 'appropriately accounted for', no data or code availability statement, and REB approval noted but consent waiver status not discussed. Minor transcription artifact ([REDACTED] fragment in methods).

novelty_literature.justification: The paper adds a large Canadian dataset to an already robust literature on OBCS vs lumpectomy oncologic safety. Findings (equivalent DFS, slight radiotherapy delay, higher minor complications) confirm existing systematic reviews and meta-analyses (refs 14, 52, 56, 34). The authors claim this is the 'largest-scale Canadian analysis', which is incremental rather than novel. Stratification by OBCS Level I vs II adds some granularity but is not a new methodological contribution.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with clear methods, detailed tables, and a balanced Discussion that directly engages with conflicting prior literature. Figures (KM plots) are appropriately referenced. Limitations are transparently discussed. Minor issues: some numerical inconsistencies (e.g., reported chemotherapy percentages 40.0% vs 40.1%), a couple of typos (p > 0.0.5'), and redundancy in the Discussion. Overall polished and publication-ready.

key_strengths: Large single-institution cohort (n=1290) with prospectively maintained database and explicit STROBE adherence
Dual independent data abstraction with third-reviewer adjudication
Direct comparison of OBCS (Level I and II) vs lumpectomy with ~10-year maximum follow-up
Clinically meaningful results: equivalent DFS and positive margins despite OBCS group having larger, more multifocal tumours
Thoughtful discussion of conflicting prior literature and the contribution of symmetry procedures to complications
key_concerns: No multivariable adjustment or propensity matching despite major baseline imbalances (age, tumor size, multifocality, neoadjuvant therapy, follow-up length)
Complication reporting at patient level prevents attribution to oncologic vs contralateral symmetry procedures
No breast-cancer-specific survival; only DFS defined narrowly as time to locoregional recurrence
Shorter median follow-up in the OBCS arm may underestimate late recurrences
Findings largely confirm prior meta-analyses, limiting novelty beyond the Canadian context
Data availability not addressed; institutional data not shared
chief_reviewer.rationale: Clinically useful, large, well-reported single-center retrospective analysis that confirms oncologic safety of OBCS; fits a tier-3 breast-surgery or surgical-oncology journal after minor revisions to add multivariable adjustment or propensity matching and clarify data sharing.
